label: a
rationale: Whole scheme-theory category (batches 6 and 7: 76 + 57 = 133 items) kept with one Alpha, as the category rule requires; both pages (diagonals/separated morphisms and Kahler differentials/conormal sequences on one side, Cech cohomology and comparison on the other) are shared-machinery neighbours and one Alpha should see both. This is one of the run's three indivisible large blocks: batch 6 alone is 76 items, the cap is three batches, and neither batch can be split or renumbered, so no partition of this run can push the largest group total below 133. No third batch is attached, which keeps this block from growing past 133 and inflating the maximum; the residual 133-vs-81 spread in this partition is that indivisible-block limit, not something Step 2 can rebalance.

label: b
rationale: Whole representation-theory category (batches 9, 10, 11: 30 + 63 + 40 = 133 items) kept with one Alpha. Three batches is the per-group cap and batch 10 (63 items) is the run's second-largest batch, so this block is indivisible in the same way as the scheme-theory block; it is that block's load twin at 133 items and cannot take extra batches. The three pages (projective extensions and the little-group method, monomial characters and M-groups, Frobenius groups and the normal complement theorem, the modular function and L1 group algebras, symmetric-group combinatorics, Bruhat decomposition over finite fields) form one coherent character-theory and finite-group-representation thread.

label: c
rationale: Whole braid-groups category (batches 15, 16, 17: 42 + 38 + 36 = 116 items) kept with one Alpha; three batches fill the cap, so the category cannot be enlarged and cannot absorb the batch-14 items its members consume. Batches 16 and 17 hold the run's largest cross-batch dependency block (16 to 14 with 7 edges, 17 to 14 with 1 edge). Those edges necessarily cross a group boundary because homological-algebra batch 14 cannot join this full three-batch group; the assignment rule places load balance first and cross-group edge minimisation last, and 116 is already within 17 items of the run's 133 ceiling.

label: d
rationale: Commutative-algebra batches 4 and 5 (32 + 18 = 50 items) must stay together and need exactly one more batch to reach the balanced floor, and algebraic-geometry batch 3 (31 items) is the coherent choice: its page algebraic-differentials-separability-and-smooth-local-presentations is commutative-algebraic in substance and its items resolve against the same machinery batches 4 and 5 carry (cor-noether-normalisation-module-finiteness, thm-auslander-buchsbaum-serre-regularity-criterion, thm-regular-sequences-give-acyclic-koszul-complexes, the Koszul and flatness criteria of the normalization and Zariski-main pages). Group total 31 + 32 + 18 = 81 items, the partition's smallest and the one intended to approach - not to fall below - the balance floor. Using the other 31-item singleton here would leave the same total while splitting the algebra cluster, and the 6-to-3 dependency (3 edges) crosses groups in every layout that respects the balance optimum; pulling batch 3 into the scheme-theory group would raise the maximum total to 164.

label: e
rationale: Load-driven residual group: combinatorics batch 1 (12 items), algebraic-topology batch 2 (31 items) and foundations batch 13 (45 items) total 88, which is the split of the five remaining singletons that keeps both remainder groups at 88 and lifts the partition's smallest group to 81. The eight non-block batches can be covered by three groups only as 3 + 3 + 2 batches, and every layout that keeps commutative algebra whole and respects the three-batch cap and the 133 maximum has a smallest group of at most 81 items; this partition attains that bound (totals 133, 133, 116, 81, 88, 88). Cross-category coherence here is weak and is accepted only because the assignment rule ranks balance above residual affinity; the three categories are single-batch categories that cannot be split anyway, and no in-run cross-batch edge touches batches 1, 2 or 13 (the only declared edges are 16 to 14, 17 to 14 and 6 to 3).

label: f
rationale: Computability-theory batch 12 (62 items) and homological-algebra batch 14 (26 items) total 88, the companion 88 of the residual split described under group e; this places the largest remaining singleton with the smallest one so that neither remainder group drops toward the 50-item commutative-algebra block. The pairing is justified by load, not by doctrine: batch 14's mathematically closest neighbour in this run is actually batch 2 (both reduce complexes over rings by elementary basis changes - contraction torsion, cell slides and stabilizations realizing elementary group-ring matrices, versus homological Gaussian elimination on invertible differential blocks), but a 2 + 14 group holds only 57 items, which would cut the partition's smallest group by 24 items and widen the spread from 52 to 76. Batch 14 stays in f so the cross-batch edges 16 to 14 and 17 to 14 are the only ones involving it, and batch 12 has no in-run cross-batch edge at all.
